question: An engineer must remove the running configuration of a Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switch and replace it with a backup file without restarting the switch. The backup file is stored on an SFTP server that is reachable via the mgmt0 interface. Which set of commands accomplishes this task?
options:
configure replace sftp://admin@192.168.10.100/backup.cfg vrf mgmt0
copy running-config bootflash://startup-config

copy sftp://admin@192.168.10.100/backup.cfg bootflash://backup.cfg vrf management
configure replace bootflash://backup.cfg

copy sftp://admin@192.168.10.100/backup.cfg startup-config vrf mgmt0
copy startup-config running-config

copy sftp://admin@192.168.10.100/backup.cfg startup-config vrf management
reload in 10
theory: The NX-OS configure replace feature compares a saved configuration file against the currently running configuration and applies only the incremental differences needed to converge the running config to match the file, all without a reload, unlike copying a file to startup-config and rebooting. Because the backup file sits on a remote SFTP server, it first needs to be copied locally to bootflash over the mgmt0 VRF, since that's the interface with SFTP reachability, before configure replace can reference it as a local file — configure replace cannot pull an sftp:// URL directly, and copying to startup-config plus copying startup to running doesn't reconcile a running configuration cleanly the way configure replace does. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 6 — NX-OS Configuration Replace and Backup Restoration)
